label: Liver immune resident component
reason: This term describes a functional population of immune cells residing in the liver, not an anatomical structure or structural subdivision. UBERON covers anatomical structures, while cellular populations and immune cell types belong in the Cell Ontology (CL) or specialized immunology ontologies. While liver lobule (UBERON:0004647) is a valid anatomical structure, 'immune resident component' refers to the collection of immune cells (Kupffer cells, NK cells, NKT cells, dendritic cells) that inhabit liver tissue - this is a cellular/immunological classification rather than a structural subdivision.
suggestion: This term should be represented in the Cell Ontology (CL) or as a defined class using CL terms with 'part_of some liver' or 'part_of some liver lobule' relationships. The three DOI references (10.1111/imm.12888, 10.1172/jci.insight.90063, 10.3389/fimmu.2019.01502) are immunology papers that would be appropriate for CL term definitions describing liver-resident immune cell populations. If an anatomical term is needed, consider whether the source data refers to a distinct anatomical compartment (like 'portal tract' UBERON:0001282) rather than a cell population.
